image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Six-storey modern Thai low-rise condominium, white rendered box with tall vertical grey fin panels between floor-to-ceiling tinted windows, recessed balconies with frosted glass balustrades staggered in a checkerboard pattern, a double-height ground-floor lobby with a projecting flat entrance canopy on slim steel posts, a landscaped planter strip along the base, a roof deck with a slatted timber screen hiding air-conditioning plant, and a small illuminated project name sign beside the entrance Materials: clean white render, matte dark-grey aluminium composite fins, tinted grey low-iron glass, frosted glass balustrades, light timber-look aluminium slats on the roof screen, brushed stainless canopy posts.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.90: silhouette 0.94 on a band table at 0.031 / 0.030 of height with every residual traced to the flank bodies' percentile, the screen placement and a thin canopy; structure 0.93 with every identity feature present at the plate's count and position; form 0.88, material 0.85 and lighting 0.86 held down by the lifted fin tone, generic planting and the invented -Z / +X elevations. 18844/32,000 triangles, 13/24 draw calls, 11/16 materials, 13/32 unique geometries.

featureReviews.evidence: Six bays of 2.5 m between three 0.3 m fins, two 1.85 m louvre boxes and 0.45 m corner fins at the proxy's +Z depth-map positions (x 40/170/300/385/510/630/720/850/985 px at 47.06 px/m), five floors at 2.85 m over a 3.05 m ground floor from its slab lines; fin faces dark on light aluminium returns, louvre slats proud of a dark plate. Band table: mean |delta width| 0.031 of height, all of it the flank louvre bodies' 95th-percentile face.
featureReviews.notes: The list-time note called the balconies a checkerboard; the plate's per-bay zoom shows the balustrade in bays B, C and E on all five floors and grid windows in A, D and F, and that is what is built. The first build's fins were dark all round and read as stripes; the plate's light returns are now aluminium bodies under 0.05 m dark face plates. Fins authored at luma 85 / sat 0.26 against the plate's 59-73 so the segmenter holds them on chroma.

featureReviews.evidence: Thirty balconies as real 1.5 m holes through two facade extrusions with a frosted balustrade (opacity 0.62) at the front plane and recessed glazing at the back, thirty grid windows with two mullions, a transom and a sill 0.15 m inside the plane. Turntable gate passes at every azimuth with 0.4-0.6 percent enclosed background, all of it batten gaps on the roof.
featureReviews.notes: The recess back walls carry a 0.70 linear vertex tint so the grid reads as recesses under the harness's flat light. The first glazing canvas was too pale and made the windows read as frosted; the stripes are now at 0.22-0.30 alpha over the teal ground, which is what the plate's dark panes with faint curtains look like at prop distance.

featureReviews.evidence: A 1.1 m coping cap 0.35 m proud (the plate's band reads 46-51 px at 39 px/m), the deck inside it, and a 580-batten timber screen 3.15 m tall spanning x -8.7..8.7 and z -6.5..2.5 with two partitions and a 3.55 x 2.4 m lift head directly behind the front run, its top 0.3 m under the rail.
featureReviews.notes: The proxy puts the screen on the rear 40 percent of the roof (front run 7.7 m behind the facade, band 9 depth 0.282 H); the plate shows the front run's full base with a 13 px deck strip in front of it where that placement would show ~80 px, and the lift head seen through the front battens, so the screen is built to the plate and carries a +0.149 band-9 residual against the proxy. The battens were widened from 0.06 to 0.075 at a 0.12 m pitch after the first turntable run measured 0.94-0.96 percent enclosed background through the gaps.

featureReviews.evidence: White-framed 5.0 m portal recessed 1.0 m with full-height glazing and a door line, a 5.6 x 2.5 m canopy at 2.4 m on two stainless posts with an edge trim, paved step, glazing runs in bays A and E-F, the BAAN JAI CONDO board on bay B, planters with a twenty-shrub hedge and six fan palms; on -X the louvre pair at z -3.0..-1.2 and 0.2..2.0 with a glazed gap, five ledges and a five-window strip.
featureReviews.notes: Flank positions from the proxy's -X map (x 235/320/390/480/500 px from the rear face at 40). The planting is the plate's greens on generic shrubs, not its species. The rear and +X elevations are authored, not observed, at 0.60 confidence.

featureReviews.evidence: Eleven materials, all measured off the plate at PBR confidence 0.734-0.860; white #ECECEC render, #445A5C fins, #4C6B68 glass, #C6D4D0 frosted balustrades, #B39B7F timber, #8F8A80 stainless.
featureReviews.notes: The fins ship lifted and teal-grey rather than the plate's charcoal (#404C49 / #353C41) because both measured tones sit inside the turntable backdrop band; the lift is recorded on the material. The glass ships at #4C6B68 above its measured #485B57 for the same reason.

name: Low-Rise Condominium
nameTh: คอนโดโลว์ไรส์
notes: The developer-built 'low-rise condo' of the last fifteen years, the third of four six-storey residential shells and the designed, clean-lined one. Sizing: six floors at 3.2 m plus a 1.2 m roof-deck screen and a taller 3.6 m lobby floor gives 21 m; six 4 m bays give 24 m and a double-loaded corridor with 7 m deep units gives 16 m. Exterior shell only, no interior geometry: the full-height glazing and the double-height lobby are tinted near-opaque panes (opacity about 0.92, low roughness) so they read as glass rather than holes, and the roof deck is a flat slab behind a screen, not a usable level. The checkerboard balcony stagger is what distinguishes it from the cream rental block and means the balcony module is instanced at alternating bays rather than every bay. Tinted grey glass and the dark fins are exactly the band the turntable backdrop's luma of 58 sits in, so both must be authored lifted and the white render must dominate the silhouette; the render is deliberately white to keep the mean luma high. SIZE CORRECTED 2026-08-27 before the build: the Meshy v7 proxy of the plate normalises to w:h:d = 1.036 : 1 : 0.842, so at the declared h = 21.0 the bounding box is 21.8 x 21.0 x 17.7; its body reads 20.5 m wide (965 px at 47.06 px/m on the +Z depth map) by 14.0 m deep with the side louvre boxes 0.65 m proud on each flank (21.8) and the entrance canopy and planter 2.2 m in front (16.55 built). The list-time 24 x 16 was a six-bay-at-4 m estimate; the proxy and plate agree on six bays of 2.5 m between 0.3 m fins, two 1.85 m louvre boxes and 0.45 m corner fins. Levels from the proxy: ground 3.05 m, five floors at 2.85 m (slab lines at 3.26 / 6.13 / 8.89 / 11.76 / 14.63 / 17.49 m), roof slab 17.75, parapet coping to 18.5, timber screen 17.75..21.0 on the REAR 40 percent of the roof (front run 7.7 m behind the facade). FACADE GRAMMAR CORRECTED from the plate: it is NOT a checkerboard -- bays A, D and F carry grid windows on every floor and bays B, C and E carry a glass-balustrade balcony on every floor, so the balcony module is instanced per bay column, not per alternating bay. Built bounding box 21.84 x 21.0 x 17.32: z from -7.72 (rear louvre slats, mirrored from the front) to +9.6 (entrance paving under a 2.5 m canopy), so d is declared 17.3.
